question.text:
Let the random variable $Y$ be defined as \[ Y = Z_1^2+Z_2^2+\cdots + Z_{9}^2 \] where $Z_i\sim N(0,1)$ for $1\leq i\leq 9.$ Find the value $y$ such that $P(Y\leq y) = 0.90.$

Hint: The table below gives the values of $x$ that satisfy $P(X\geq x) = p,$ where $X\sim \chi^2(k).$

$k \setminus p$ $0.010$ $0.050$ $0.100$ $0.150$ $0.200$
$ 9 $ $\,21.666\,$ $\,16.919\,$ $\,14.684\,$ $\,13.288\,$ $\,12.242\,$
$ 10 $ $\,23.209\,$ $\,18.307\,$ $\,15.987\,$ $\,14.534\,$ $\,13.442\,$
$ 11 $ $\,24.725\,$ $\,19.675\,$ $\,17.275\,$ $\,15.767\,$ $\,14.631\,$
question.explanation:
If $Z_i\sim N(0,1)$ for $1\leq i \leq k$ are independent normal random variables, then the sum \[ Z_1^2+Z_2^2+\cdots + Z_{k}^2 \] follows a $\chi^2(k)$ distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom.

So, in our case, we have

\[ Y = Z_1^2+Z_2^2+\cdots + Z_{9}^2 \sim \chi^2(9). \]

First, we express the given probability in the form $P(Y\geq y){:}$

\begin{align*} P(Y\leq y) &= 1-P(Y\geq y) \\[5pt] 0.90 &= 1-P(Y\geq y) \\[5pt] P(Y\geq y) &=0.10 \end{align*}

Now, we wish to find the value $y$ such that $P(Y\geq y) = 0.10$ This can be found from the given table:

$k \setminus p$ $0.010$ $0.050$ $0.100$ $0.150$ $0.200$
$ 9 $ $\,21.666\,$ $\,16.919\,$ $\,\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{14.684}\,$ $\,13.288\,$ $\,12.242\,$
$ 10 $ $\,23.209\,$ $\,18.307\,$ $\,15.987\,$ $\,14.534\,$ $\,13.442\,$
$ 11 $ $\,24.725\,$ $\,19.675\,$ $\,17.275\,$ $\,15.767\,$ $\,14.631\,$

So, we have

\[ P(Y\geq 14.684) = 0.10 \] which means \[ P(Y\leq 14.684) = 0.90. \]

Therefore, $y=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{14.684}.$
